title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the previous one ('Deux questions de p.d.'). There A is a coassociative k-coalgebra and (B,J) a PD-algebra. The convolution algebra Hom_k(A,B) contains the ideal Hom_k(A,J), and the question was whether that ideal carries divided powers. Grothendieck now lists candidate equivalent kinds of extra structure on A that would make this work, functorially. I read items 3-6 as a chain of equivalent definitions he intended to compare; the page itself does not state the equivalence.

(3) For every k-module M and p ≥ 0, a non-linear map u_p : Hom_k(A,M) → Hom_k(A,Γ^p M), written f ↦ f^(p), natural in M. It should satisfy:
- f^(0) = 1 (the counit followed by k = Γ^0 M);
- f^(1) = f;
- (f+g)^(p) = Σ_{i+j=p} f^(i) g^(j), the product being convolution in Hom_k(A, Γ^• M);
- (λf)^(p) = λ^p f^(p).
He notes, correctly, that the last rule is automatic: it follows from naturality applied to multiplication by λ on M, which acts by λ^p on Γ^p M. By a Yoneda / polynomial-law argument, such a family is determined by the universal case M = A, f = id_A. This gives maps u_p : A → Γ^p A, which are exactly the u_n = u_1^(n) of question ② on the previous page, with f^(p) = Γ^p(f) ∘ u_p. The exponential rule is then a 'divided-power comultiplication' axiom on A.

(4) A PD structure on Hom_k(A, Γ^+ M) ⊂ Hom_k(A, Γ^• M), natural in M. The image writes Hom_k(A,M) as the ambient ring, presumably shorthand.

(5) The universal case: a PD structure on Hom(A, Γ^+ A) ⊂ Hom(A, Γ^• A).

(6) For every PD-algebra (B,I), a PD structure on Hom_k(A,I) ⊂ Hom_k(A,B), natural in (B,I).

The passage 4 → 6 uses that Γ_k(M) is the free PD-algebra on M (Roby). Any PD-algebra (B,I) receives a PD-morphism Γ_k(I) → B, and naturality transports the structure. The passage 3 → 4 is the usual extension of 'γ_p on a set of generators satisfying the sum rule' to a full PD structure.

The natural answer to the question: if A is cocommutative and k-flat, the iterated coproduct Δ_p : A → (A^{⊗p})^{S_p} ≅ Γ^p A supplies u_p. The divided powers on Hom(A,I) are then f^{[p]} = (Γ^p I → I) ∘ Γ^p(f) ∘ Δ_p. For finite free A this agrees with the extension of the PD structure on J along the flat map B → A^∨ ⊗ B.

The purpose, given the title of the dossier (PD de Rham complex, IHÉS 1976), is presumably this: the PD envelope of the diagonal (PD principal parts) is the convolution dual Hom(D,O) of the coalgebra D of (PD-)differential operators, and its augmentation ideal should get its divided powers in exactly this way. The page breaks off after item 6 ('....').
errors: Divided powers only make sense on a commutative ideal. The previous page assumes only that A is a coassociative coalgebra; for Hom_k(A,B) to be commutative, A should be cocommutative, or the u_p must be given as data landing in symmetric tensors.

Over a general base ring k, (A^{⊗p})^{S_p} ≠ Γ^p A unless A is flat. Hence the u_p in (3) are genuine extra data ('Donnée') rather than automatic. This seems to be exactly why Grothendieck phrases 3)-6) as data; it is not an error, but the equivalences are only sketched.
In item 4 the ambient ring is written Hom_k(A,M); it must be Hom_k(A,Γ^• M), since Γ^+M is not a submodule of M.
The final equivalence 3) ⇔ 4) ⇔ 5) ⇔ 6) is listed but never stated or proved; 'et —' in item 3 and the '....' in item 6 are unfinished.

ideas.what: Divided powers on the convolution algebra Hom_k(A,B) restricted to Hom_k(A,I), for A a (cocommutative) coalgebra and (B,I) a PD-algebra
ideas.modern_name: PD structure on convolution algebras / on the dual of a divided-power coalgebra (e.g. PD principal parts as dual of PD differential operators)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (PD differential operators and PD envelopes, 1974); Roby for Γ and polynomial laws
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts as far as I know; related material in Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (LNM 407) and Berthelot–Ogus.

ideas.what: Natural non-linear maps f ↦ f^(p), Hom(A,M) → Hom(A,Γ^p M), with the exponential/sum rule, reduced to universal maps u_p : A → Γ^p A
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power (Γ-)coalgebra structure; polynomial laws (Roby); Yoneda reduction to the universal element
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (1963–65) for polynomial laws and Γ; divided power coalgebras appear later (e.g. Fresse on Γ(Com))

ideas.what: Reduction of 'functorial PD for all PD-algebras (B,I)' to the universal case (Γ^• M, Γ^+ M) and then to M = A
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of Γ_k(M) as the free PD-algebra on M

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a list of equivalent axiomatizations of a 'coalgebra whose convolution duals into PD-algebras are PD-algebras' over an arbitrary base, where flatness fails and the u_p must be extra data. He does not complete it. This is a divided-power coalgebra notion over general rings, formulated via natural transformations Hom(A,−) → Hom(A,Γ^p −).
missed.quote: Donnée, pour toute k-algèbre B (avec idéal I à p.d.), d'une loi de p.d. sur Hom_k(A,I) ⊂ Hom_k(A,B), fonctorielle en (B,I) ....
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only mildly. Divided-power coalgebras and coalgebras over Γ-type comonads appear in derived/animated PD theory and in Dieudonné theory, but the flat cocommutative case is routine. The non-flat case is presumably covered by modern simplicial/animated treatments.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but essentially routine axiomatic exploration: divided powers on convolution algebras, reduced via Yoneda and the universality of Γ. It is consistent with Berthelot/Roby-type results and was left unfinished; nothing a specialist would find unexpected.
transcription_corrections: Item 3, line 2: 'notée' is written above the arrow and the arrow label is u_p. 'aussi par f sous-entendu' is more plausibly 'ou plus brièvement' / 'notée aussi'; the crossed-out word is 'faite'/'f' (uncertain).
Item 4: the ambient is written 'Hom_k(A,M)' but mathematically must be Hom_k(A, Γ^• M).
Item 5: the struck and rewritten text reads 'Loi de p.d. sur Hom(A,Γ^+A) ⊂ Hom(A,Γ^•A)', followed by an underlined parenthetical '(cas universel)' rather than '(où ... communs)'.
Item 6: '(avec idéal I à p.d.)' — the ideal is I, written like 'J/I'.
